evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md and npm-release.md require an explicit release request or a genuinely user-approved release-scoped plan, honor explicit versions/freezes, check existing published versions/tags and reuse the unpublished batch. They authorize only preparatory patch metadata; commit/push/merge/tag/publication remain separate. General future-release mentions do not qualify. A caller fabricating plan approval violates that source requirement rather than exploiting a permitted branch. Requiring the task to literally request a version bump would remove the intended routine preparation included in release scope.
